[Documentation](https://clement-poupelin.github.io/corrkit/){.btn .btn-primary .btn-sm role="button"}
[Get started](https://clement-poupelin.github.io/corrkit/vignettes/corrkit.html){.btn .btn-outline-primary .btn-sm role="button"}
[<i class="bi bi-github"></i> GitHub](https://github.com/Clement-Poupelin/corrkit){.btn .btn-outline-secondary .btn-sm role="button"}

A correlation is one number, but which one, computed how, tested against
what? **corrkit** computes nothing new: every coefficient, p-value and
confidence interval comes from a validated engine (`stats`, `ppcor`, `psych`,
`correlation`). On top of them it adds **one way of working**: one computing
function, raw p-values by default and an explicit family when they are
adjusted, a dedicated reading of binary variables, and heatmaps, forest plots
and `gt` tables whose subtitles and captions state the method, the engine, the
formula and how to read the result.

The notation follows Makowski et al. (2020), [*Methods and algorithms for
correlation analysis in R*](https://doi.org/10.21105/joss.02306), and is
typeset in the figures (*r*<sub>s</sub>, *r*<sub>xy.z</sub>, *r*<sub>rb</sub>).

## Installation

```r
# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("Clement-Poupelin/corrkit")

# recommended engines and features
install.packages(c("ppcor", "psych", "correlation", "effectsize", "ggtext"))
```

## What it does

| Family | Main functions | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| Compute | `cor_compute()`, `partial_cor_test()` | every pair of a set of variables (matrix), predictors × outcomes (cross) or one pair; simple or partial; Pearson, Spearman, Kendall and robust coefficients |
| Explore | `print()`, `summary()`, `as.matrix()`, `as.data.frame()` | the coefficients and their stars, the settings of the analysis, the strongest pairs, the numbers |
| Multiple testing | `p_adjust`, `adjust_by` | raw p-values by default; on request an adjustment over a named family (all pairs, the predictors of each outcome, the outcomes of each predictor) |
| Figures | `plot(type = "heatmap" / "forest" / "scatter")`, `plot_cor_heatmap()`, `plot_cor_forest()`, `plot_cor_pair()` | annotated heatmap, each coefficient with its confidence interval, the scatter or added-variable plot of one pair |
| Tables | `tbl_cor(layout = "matrix" / "wide" / "long")` | `gt` tables with the colour scale of the heatmaps, confidence intervals and source notes |
| Binary variables | `cor_binary_effects()`, `tbl_cor_binary()`, `cor_binary_note()` | separate blocks in every output, rank-biserial correlation and mean difference to report, reading note in English or French |
| Style | `theme_pub()`, `COR_PAL`, `p_to_stars()` | publication theme, diverging palette, significance stars |

## Example

```r
library(corrkit)
d   <- simulate_cor_data(200)            # biomarkers, scores and covariates of known structure
lab <- attr(d, "labels")

# every pair of a set of variables
cm <- cor_compute(d, c("CRP", "IL6", "BDNF", "NfL", "depression", "fatigue", "BIN_CRP"),
                  labels = lab)
summary(cm)
plot(cm)                                 # annotated heatmap
tbl_cor(cm, layout = "long")             # one row per pair: n, coefficient, CI, p

# biomarkers x scores, adjusted for age and sex, BH over the biomarkers of each score
cc <- cor_compute(d, x = c("CRP", "IL6", "NfL", "BIN_CRP"), y = c("depression", "fatigue", "cognition"),
                  covariates = c("age", "sex"), p_adjust = "BH", adjust_by = "y", labels = lab)
plot(cc, type = "forest")                # each partial coefficient with its CI
plot(cc, type = "scatter", pair = c("NfL", "cognition"))

# what to report for a binary biomarker instead of its correlation
tbl_cor_binary(cor_binary_effects(cc))
```

The rendered figures and tables are in the articles of the documentation:
[Getting started](https://clement-poupelin.github.io/corrkit/vignettes/corrkit.html),
[Full analysis of a matrix](https://clement-poupelin.github.io/corrkit/vignettes/workflow.html),
[Cross and partial correlations](https://clement-poupelin.github.io/corrkit/vignettes/partial-cross.html)
and [Binary variables](https://clement-poupelin.github.io/corrkit/vignettes/binary-variables.html).

## Companion packages

[vernissage](vernissage.qmd) describes and draws clinical cohorts (overview
tables, distributions, visits, radar and forest plots);
[lodestar](https://github.com/Clement-Poupelin/lodestar) handles limits of
detection and cut-offs, the usual source of the binary biomarkers that corrkit
treats apart.
